title: GOVERNMENT TAKES NEXT STEP TO CUT COMPLIANCE COSTS
content:
22 September 1999

GOVERNMENT TAKES NEXT STEP TO CUT COMPLIANCE COSTS

  • Wyatt Creech
Health

The Government has taken the next step in its plans to cut compliance costs for small businesses - setting up a panel of experts to test compliance costs faced by general practitioners.

Health Minister Wyatt Creech today announced the establishment of the General Practitioner Compliance Cost Reduction Test Panel.

"Doctors have raised concerns with me about compliance costs. The Test Panel will help address the concerns."

The aim of the pilot Test Panel is to develop practical proposals to reduce general practitioner compliance costs.

The panel will be chaired by Dr Tricia Briscoe a Rotorua GP and member of the New Zealand Medical Association Board.

It will look at where coordination and collaboration between Government agencies can reduce compliance costs, simplify information requirements placed on general practitioners and claiming processes.

The pilot Test Panel will be evaluated to determine whether it is an efficient method for reducing compliance costs and identify any improvements needed for the roll out of other test panels.

This first test panel is part of the Government's Bright Futures package - which includes measures to make life simpler for small businesses by cutting red tape, and removing outdated regulations and laws.

The panels will advise the Government on the impact of proposed legislation before final Parliamentary approval.

ENDS

For further information please contact Anna Hughes (04) 4719 819 or (025) 477 987. Membership of Test Panel attached.

General Practitioner Compliance Cost Reduction Test Panel.

Dr Tricia Briscoe
Dr Briscoe is a general practitioner in Rotorua. Dr Briscoe has been a Director of the Rotorua General Practice Group IPA.

Dr Tim Baily Gibson
Dr Baily Gibson is a Masterton GP and GP Obstetrician, and has had many years experience of solo practice in a small provincial town. Dr Gibson is currently a member of the NZMA General Practice Council and the Deputy Chairman of CareNET (an association of independent general practitioners).

Dr Branko Sijnja
Dr Sijnja is a rural GP in a community owned health and hospital centre in Balclutha. He was an executive committee member for the General Practitioners Association for five years, and is currently a member of the General Practitioner Council.

Dr Kim Bannister
Dr Banister is the Honorary Secretary of the RNZCGP. Dr Bannister is an urban GP and member of the Comprehensive Health Services IPA.

Dr Vivienne R Coppell
Dr Coppell is a rural GP based at Te Puia Springs. Dr Coppell is a member of the Professional Development Committee of the RNZCGP.

Peter Glensor
Peter is the National Coordinator of Health Care Aotearoa. General practices associated with Health Care Aotearoa are community owned, with general practitioners being on a salary.

Dr David Dixon
Dr Dixon works part time in a joint practice in Nelson City and has coordinated the Nelson GPs Clearing House project for the last three years. Dr Dixon is the current Chair of CareNET and a member of the Nelson Community Health Committee.

Dr Peter Vujcich
Dr Vujcich is a long term rural GP with a wealth of experience dealing with issues relating to rural health care. Dr Vujcich is currently based in Kaikohe.

Dr Phil White
Dr White is a GP based at the Paraparaumu Medical Centre. Dr White has previously worked for the central RHA and has recently managed the Marlborough integrated care pilot.
